scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the inter-AS physical/link layer on router2 (eth0), which underpins the eBGP peering between AS1 and AS2.

Mechanism: With router2’s interconnect interface down, the L2/L1 path between the BGP peers is broken. Router2’s BGP stays in Active (no TCP session), so it learns no 195.11.14.0/24 route. Router1 cannot reach 193.10.11.2 either, so any traffic it forwards toward 200.1.1.0/24 over eth0 will fail at the link. Each PC still reaches its own gateway because the LAN interfaces (router1 eth1 and router2 eth1) are up.

Localization: On router2, eth0 is administratively/operationally down:
- ip addr shows eth0 state DOWN with 193.10.11.2/24.
- ethtool eth0 reports “Link detected: no.”
- BGP on router2: show ip bgp summary shows neighbor 193.10.11.1 in Active, PfxRcd 0.
Corroboration from the far side:
- router1 eth0 is UP, but ping 193.10.11.2 fails (100% loss), proving the inter-AS link is broken at router2’s end.

Root cause: router2’s inter-AS interface eth0 is down, breaking the single-hop eBGP session and severing cross-AS reachability.

Corrective fix:
- Bring up router2 eth0 (e.g., ip link set dev eth0 up) or fix the cabling/veth binding causing no carrier. Verify “ip link” shows UP/LOWER_UP and “ethtool” shows Link detected: yes.
- Confirm eBGP establishes (router2: Established with PfxRcd 1; router1 likewise) and that both routers install 195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24.
- Retest pc1↔pc2 reachability.
